answer: At the zenith of the PoA protocol, each AI grader receives a time‑locked token that routes its reputation score through a river of random jury assignments; only the selected jury can audit a grader’s proofs within a short audit window. The beacon of cryptographic signatures forces the grader to reveal a fresh zero‑knowledge proof for each task, which the jury verifies before confirming the grade. An attacker must generate a unique proof and stake for every forged identity, incurring linear cost proportional to the number of audits, quickly exhausting resources.
